options.ratio: 1/2 cup cream → 3/4 cup thick curd, hung in a cloth for 30 minutes. Take the pan off the heat before it goes in, and stir it through, added to a boiling gravy it will split.
options.taste_and_texture: Tangier and lighter. It will not give you the flat, heavy richness cream does, and in a dish built entirely around that richness you will notice the absence.
options.nutritional_rationale: More protein, substantially less saturated fat per serving. Comparative only.

options.swap: Soaked and ground kabuli chana paste
options.ratio: 1/2 cup cream → 1/3 cup kabuli chana, soaked overnight, boiled soft, ground smooth with a little of its water. Cook it into the gravy for five minutes.
options.taste_and_texture: Gives body rather than richness, a rounder, slightly nutty gravy that coats the same way. It is closer to how a period gravy was actually thickened than cream is.
options.nutritional_rationale: Protein and fibre both up; saturated fat well down.

where_it_went: Restaurant kitchens standardised on cream because it is fast, stable and forgiving, and the home cook followed the restaurant. Ground pulses and nuts had done the thickening before it.
